answer: A network can gate rewards behind a fresh, proctored skill exam each epoch. Every identity draws unique questions from a large pool, like water finding a new inlet each tide, and must answer under a strict time limit with cheating checks. A falcon cannot hunt in two skies at once, and neither can one operator sit ten exams at once: each fake identity needs its own skilled human, so cost grows linearly while rewards stay flat. Scores rest on a knoll of verified competence, not on copied credentials, and failures freeze payouts until the next round.
